abstract: Biomass-based conductive aerogels with excellent biocompatibility, high porosity, and facile functionalization are the key materials for new-generation sustainable high-performance piezoresistive sensors. However, the single lamellar structure of conventional aerogels and the inherent agglomeration tendency of conductive nanomaterials severely hamper the mechanical and strain sensing properties of biomass-based aerogels. Herein, inspired by the natural bamboo-node structure, a novel gelation-confinement strategy was developed to construct a unique bamboo-node-reinforced structure by incorporating metallogels (MOGs) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into cellulose nanofibers (CNFs). The resulting CNF-based aerogel exhibits excellent mechanical stability and can withstand over 5000 compression cycles at 50% strain. Meanwhile, integration of the aerogel into a flexible piezoresistive sensor endows the device with comprehensive strain sensing properties, including high linear sensitivity (S = 4.14 kPa -1 in the 0-2 kPa range; S = 1.88 kPa -1 in the 2-92 kPa range) and a low-pressure detection limit of 2.21 Pa. These multifunctional features endow the composite aerogel with great application potential in motion monitoring.

title: Editorial Board
Protonated chitosan/poly(ε-caprolactone) graft copolymer coatings for pH-modulated release of phosphorus fertilizers
abstract: This study reports the synthesis of protonated chitosan-g-poly(ε-caprolactone) copolymers and their use as pH-modulated coatings for the controlled release of phosphorus from granular monoammonium phosphate (MAP) and diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertilizers. Copolymers were synthesized in two steps: first, chitosan amino groups were protonated using dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl) to limit their participation in the polymerization reaction; then, ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of ε-caprolactone was performed from the hydroxyl groups using tin(II) 2-ethylhexanoate (Sn(Oct) 2 ) at 120 °C. Five copolymers were synthesized with increasing proportions of chitosan-HCl (2%, 3%, 5%, 7% and 10%). The materials were applied as polymeric coatings on MAP and DAP fertilizers using a rotary pan technique. Phosphorus release kinetics were studied in sandy and aqueous media under varying pH conditions. The results demonstrate a significant delay in phosphorus release from coated MAP and DAP compared with uncoated systems or those coated with neat poly(ε-caprolactone), with release behaviour influenced by the surrounding pH.

title: Janus CMC-based hydrogel with multifunctional synergy for hemostasis and wound healing
abstract: Timely hemostasis, bacterial inhibition, and accelerated tissue regeneration are core demands for clinical wound care. However, integrating robust wet adhesion and surface antifouling performance simultaneously remains a key bottleneck limiting conventional wound dressings. Herein, a carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)-based drug-loaded hydrogel (DLCH) co-embedded with polyhexamethylene biguanide-loaded zeolite (PHMB@Zeo) and gelatin-dopamine-stabilized silver nanoparticles (Gel-DA-AgNPs) was rationally developed as the bottom functional therapeutic layer. Further, an asymmetric Janus drug-loaded hydrogel (JDLH) was fabricated by modifying DLCH surface with a hydrophobic HMDSO-TiO₂ antifouling coating. As the functional core, DLCH exhibits 45 kPa wet adhesion, 1353% stretchability, and sustained PHMB release over 240 h, achieving > 99% antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus. Benefiting from DLCH's intrinsic superior properties, the resulting JDLH achieves rapid hemostasis at 41.33 ± 7.97 s and 46.33 ± 9.79 s in rat liver and heart non-compressible hemorrhage models, respectively. In vivo assays verify that JDLH accelerates full-thickness skin wound repair, reaching a 99.5% closure ratio on day 15 with boosted collagen deposition and angiogenesis. This work presents a portable Janus dressing with asymmetric adhesion, offering a practical advance for polysaccharide-based wound dressings and a promising candidate for emergency trauma and clinical wound care.

title: Structure-activity comparison of native larch arabinogalactan and its arabinose-depleted derivative in D-galactose-induced aging-like mice
abstract: Inflammaging is closely associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, and structurally complex polysaccharides may provide microbiota-directed protection. This study compared the protective effects and gut microbiota-metabolite responses of native larch arabinogalactan (AG) and an acid-hydrolyzed arabinose-depleted derivative (DA) in D-galactose-induced aging-like mice. AG is a highly branched galactose (Gal)- and arabinose (Ara)-rich polysaccharide with a 1,3-linked Galp backbone and Galp/Ara-containing side chains. Acid hydrolysis markedly depleted Ara residues while largely retaining the Gal-rich branched framework, but also altered molecular size and solution-level properties. Both AG and DA alleviated oxidative-inflammatory responses, behavioral and multi-organ aging-like alterations, P53/P21-associated senescence-related responses, and colonic mucus barrier impairment. Direct dose-matched comparisons showed no significant AG-DA differences for most major host endpoints, while dose-response patterns varied across outcomes rather than showing a uniform monotonic trend. Cecal microbiota analyses revealed overlapping but treatment-biased responses, with AG associated with greater Bifidobacterium enrichment and DA with stronger Turicibacter enrichment. Exploratory metabolomic and pathway analyses further suggested partially convergent bile acid/lipid-related responses together with treatment-biased metabolic patterns. These findings suggest that Ara-depletion-associated structural changes are linked to treatment-biased microbiota-metabolite responses, whereas the retained Gal-rich branched framework may contribute to the protective effects observed with both treatments.

title: A Paris polysaccharide adjuvant enhances vaccine immunogenicity via activating antigen-presenting cells in peripheral tissue and lymph nodes
abstract: The limited availability of safe and effective vaccine adjuvants remains a major bottleneck in modern vaccinology, particularly for inducing balanced and robust cellular and humoral immune responses. This study investigated the adjuvant potential of polysaccharides isolated from Paris mairei (PMM, 740 kDa) and Paris yunnanensis (PPM, 92 kDa). Structural analysis confirmed that both polysaccharides are primarily composed of a (1 → 4)-linked β-D-Man backbone with mannose residues partially acetylated at the O-2 or O-3 positions. However, only PMM effectively activated antigen-presenting cells (APCs). In combination with aluminum hydroxide (AH), PMM enhanced both IgG1 and IgG2a humoral responses and promoted Th1-associated cellular immune responses in Varicella-zoster virus glycoprotein E (VZV gE) models. Mechanistic studies revealed that AH functions as a local antigen depot, while soluble PMM accumulates in draining lymph nodes to activate APCs. PMM-induced macrophage activation involves TLR4 signaling, accompanied by NF-κB/MAPK activation and M1 polarization. This study identifies Paris-derived polysaccharides as promising innate immune modulators and provides a feasible polysaccharide-AH combination strategy for improving vaccine adjuvant design.

title: Adaptive topological networks enabled by high-aspect-ratio cellulose nanofibrils for robust and self-healing hydrogel wearable sensors
abstract: Flexible wearable sensors for personalized healthcare and human-machine interaction require substrates combining high mechanical strength, rapid self-healing, and stable electro-conductivity. However, existing materials suffer from intrinsic trade-offs among these properties. Inspired by biological networks, we introduce a conceptual paradigm of adaptive topological networks (ATN) enabled by high-aspect-ratio cellulose nanofibrils (HAR-CNF, ~230). Unlike conventional fillers, our ATN framework positions HAR-CNF as a topological "entropy modulator" and "mechano-chemical coupling agent" orchestrating the interplay among three networks: a HAR-CNF physical entanglement network, a borate ester dynamic covalent network, and a silver nanowires (AgNWs) percolation network. This architecture resolves the trade-offs through three synergistic mechanisms-topological entropy modulation for energy dissipation, force-assisted dynamic bond reassembly for ultra-fast healing (99.5% efficiency, 2 min), and hierarchical confinement with a slip-lock mechanism for ultra-wide-range sensing (0-1000% strain). The hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of 238 kPa and an elongation at break of 1600%. The assembled sensor exhibits high sensitivity (gauge factor = 6.74, pressure sensitivity = 0.583 kPa -1 ), rapid response (179 ms), and stable cycling over 1000 s, enabling monitoring of facial micro-expressions, joint motions, and spatial pressure mapping via a 5 × 5 sensing array. This ATN paradigm offers a transformative platform for high-reliability flexible electronic skins.

title: Cellulose nanocrystal-templated synthesis and distribution of carbon dots to construct covalent networks with enhanced photostability for light management applications
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) suffer from poor photostability in light-conversion applications, as physical encapsulation fails to suppress photo-oxidation due to weak interfacial interactions. To address this, a covalent interface engineering strategy is developed to induce the in situ synthesis of CDs on cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) as a template. Via one-step amidation and silylation, a covalently grafted network structure, CNC-templated CDs (CNC-CDs), is constructed, which suppresses aggregation-induced quenching and enhances the solid-state quantum yield of CDs from 1.67% to 10.08%. CNC-CDs utilize a CNC framework to promote electron transfer and suppress electron-hole recombination by adjusting the band structure, thereby reducing the generation of singlet oxygen. The resulting CNC-CDs/PVA film integrates spectral conversion (from CDs) and light scattering (from CNCs), leading to a 10.43% increase in red-light photon flux density and a 24.2% enhancement of the Hill reaction rate in isolated chloroplasts. Lettuce cultivation shows that covering plants with this film increases fresh weight by 23.41% and dry weight by 18.91%. This study provides a new interfacial design strategy for highly stable, multifunctional light-conversion materials.

title: β-Cyclodextrin-based composites for wastewater treatment: Recent advances, challenges, and future perspectives
abstract: β-Cyclodextrin (β-CD) is a versatile supramolecular host whose hydrophobic cavity and chemically accessible exterior enable selective interactions with diverse contaminants. However, the limited recoverability, structural stability, and reusability of free β-CD restrict its direct application in aqueous treatment systems. Immobilization, crosslinking, and hybridization with polymers, biomass, carbonaceous materials, magnetic particles, metal-organic and covalent organic frameworks, photocatalysts, and membrane substrates improve porosity, mechanical stability, separation, and pollutant-removal performance. This review critically examines advances in β-CD-based composites for removing pharmaceuticals, dyes, pesticides, heavy metals, PFAS, and other emerging contaminants from water and wastewater reported between 2021 and 2026. Attention is given to structure-performance relationships, host-guest inclusion and complementary interfacial interactions, adsorption, photocatalytic degradation, membrane separation, regeneration, and performance in complex water matrices. Emerging computational approaches, including density functional theory, molecular dynamics, molecular docking, and artificial intelligence, are also discussed in relation to molecular-level interpretation, performance prediction, and process optimization. Finally, the review evaluates the principal barriers to practical implementation, including non-standardized testing, limited continuous-flow and real-wastewater validation, component leaching, regeneration-related waste, synthesis cost, scalability, and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. This integrated perspective provides guides the development of more effective, durable, and practically viable β-CD-based water-treatment materials.

title: Pore-filling engineering of all-biomass cellulose/thymol films via solvent-induced phase inversion for moisture-barrier and antibacterial fruit preservation
abstract: Plastic pollution and postharvest food loss have intensified the demand for high-performance biodegradable packaging, yet regenerated cellulose films are limited by a porous Cellulose II architecture and high moisture sensitivity. Here, a robust all-biomass film is developed by incorporating thymol into a bamboo-derived cellulose matrix via solvent-induced phase inversion. During solvent exchange, thymol crystallizes in situ and fills the inherent micropores, stabilized by interfacial hydrogen bonding, transforming the porous network into a dense, high-barrier interface. This pore-filling selectively suppresses the polar surface-energy component, raising the water contact angle from 43° to 68° (61° for the optimized CT-0.3) and lowering the water vapor permeability by around 53%, thereby resolving the trade-off between breathability and moisture barrier without sacrificing mechanical integrity (tensile strength around 46 MPa at around 12 μm). Molecular dynamics simulations show thymol to be dynamically anchored, undergoing humidity-dependent, chain-selective redistribution without bulk desorption. The optimized film exhibits potent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, reducing viable bacteria by around 60-90%, with sustained, near-zero-order thymol release. Applied to strawberries and bananas, it inhibits weight loss and delays senescence, extending shelf life to seven days (over double the pristine-cellulose control), offering a promising platform for all-biomass active packaging.

title: Polypyrrole nanomorphology-driven sodium alginate based multifunctional hydrogels: Synergistic integration of mechanical robustness, electromagnetic shielding, and strain sensing
abstract: Conductive hydrogels integrating mechanical reinforcement, electromagnetic shielding, and sensing functions have attracted considerable attention for multifunctional wearable electronics. Herein, a morphology-controlled polypyrrole (PPy) strategy was proposed to fabricate biochar (BC)-reinforced sodium alginate (SA) and polyacrylamide (PAM) semi-interpenetrating polymer network (semi-IPN) multifunctional conductive hydrogels. The results showed that the tubular PPy-based composite hydrogel, denoted as BSPH@PPy-Tube exhibited enhanced strength, stretchability, and toughness, with a tensile strength of 1.00 MPa, an elongation at break of 1486.43%, a modulus of 0.07 GPa, and a tensile toughness of 8.14 MJ·m -3 . This improvement was attributed to the synergistic network among tubular PPy, BC, and the SA and PAM matrix, where tubular PPy served as conductive bridges and stress-transfer pathways, while hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and π-π stacking strengthen the interfacial interactions within the hydrogel. The interconnected tubular PPy and BC conductive network promoted electron transport, interfacial polarization, and multiple electromagnetic wave attenuation, achieving an EMI shielding effectiveness of 46.19 dB. The BSPH@PPy-Tube was further assembled as a flexible strain sensor, exhibiting a gauge factor of 5.07 in the 100-200% strain range and stable electrical responses to human motions. This work provides a feasible strategy for constructing multifunctional conductive hydrogels with mechanical robustness, electromagnetic protection, and wearable sensing capability.

title: Metal ion coordination-crosslinked polysaccharides: Emerging platforms for advanced drug delivery
abstract: Natural polysaccharides are attractive drug delivery materials owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and structural tunability. However, conventional polysaccharide-based systems often exhibit limited structural and mechanical stability, insufficient drug-loading capacity, and inadequate regulation of drug release. Metal-ion coordination-mediated crosslinking of polysaccharides endows polysaccharide-based delivery systems with desirable properties such as self-assembly, adhesion, and mechanical tunability, thereby improving drug-loading efficiency, structural stability, and controlled drug release. Moreover, the physicochemical properties and intrinsic biological activities of metal ions may further confer polysaccharide-based systems with additional functions, including antibacterial, antioxidant, catalytic, photothermal, and osteogenic functions. This review summarizes the molecular coordination mechanisms, coordination properties and biological roles of representative metal ions, metal-ion coordination-enabled polysaccharide delivery platforms and their fabrication strategies, as well as coordination-driven improvements in drug loading, responsive release, and functional integration. Finally, challenges associated with batch-to-batch consistency, long-term biosafety, and clinical translation are discussed, together with future opportunities in AI-driven and adaptive design of metal-coordinated polysaccharide platforms.

title: Generational shifts in thiolated cyclodextrins: Toward more efficient drug delivery systems
abstract: Thiolated cyclodextrins represent a rapidly evolving class of multifunctional excipients that extend the role of cyclodextrins beyond solubilization toward active participation in mucosal drug delivery. By integrating the inclusion complexation capacity of cyclodextrins with the reactivity of thiol groups, these systems can enhance drug residence time on target tissues, epithelial permeation, and cellular uptake. This review discusses the generational evolution of thiolated cyclodextrins, from first-generation derivatives bearing free sulfhydryl groups to advanced S-protected systems designed to improve stability, control reactivity, and enable deeper mucus penetration. Particular emphasis is placed on how second- and third-generation thiolated cyclodextrins overcome key limitations of conventional thiomers, including premature oxidation and superficial binding to the rapidly cleared mucus layer. We further highlight their emerging role as performance-enhancing excipients in oral, ocular, respiratory, and other mucosal delivery platforms, such as nanocarrier systems. By linking structural modification, mucoadhesion, mucus penetration, and absorption-enhancing mechanisms, this review provides a forward-looking perspective on thiolated cyclodextrins as next-generation tools for designing more efficient and biologically responsive drug delivery systems.

title: Modulation of in vitro digestibility and gut microbiota fermentation profiles of different V-type starch-resveratrol complexes fabricated via heat-moisture treatment
abstract: V-type starch (type 5 resistant starch, RS5) is a promising dietary component for metabolic health, yet structure-function relationships among its crystalline subtypes under polyphenol modulation remain unclear. In this study, three V-type starch variants (V6, V7 and V8) and their resveratrol (RA) complexes were prepared via heat-moisture treatment (HMT) using ethanol, tert-butanol and salicylic acid as guest molecules. The multi-scale structures, in vitro digestibility, molecular interaction and fecal fermentation characteristics were systematically evaluated. XRD confirmed the successful induction of V6, V7, and V8 crystalline patterns. RA incorporation dose-dependently increased relative crystallinity and V-type crystal content. V8 complexes exhibited the highest RA complexation ratio and resistant starch content (28.03%), whereas V7 complexes preferentially formed slowly digestible starch. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that salicylic acid possessed the strongest binding affinity to amylose, and the stable V8 helical cavity accommodated two RA molecules via hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions. In vitro fecal fermentation demonstrated that V6 and V8 complexes significantly boosted short-chain fatty acid production and enriched beneficial Faecalibacterium and Bifidobacterium, whereas V7 complexes stimulated opportunistic pathogens (Escherichia and Citrobacter). These findings clarify the molecular basis of V-type starch-polyphenol interactions, providing a rational framework for designing starch-based functional foods.

title: Novel pyrimidine nucleoside - chitosan - silybin micelles for improving the oral absorption of doxorubicin via intestinal nucleoside transporter
abstract: A kind of novel pyrimidine nucleoside (PYN) and silybin (SB) conjugated chitosan (CS) (PYN-CS-SB) polymer micelles were designed for enhancing the oral absorption of doxorubicin (DOX) via the nucleoside transporters located at intestinal epithelial cell. The four types of endogenous PYNs selected respectively as the ligands of the transporter, along with SB, were conjugated to CS. The PYN-CS-SB were synthesized and identified by 1 H NMR and FT-IR. The drug-loaded micelles were prepared by ultrasound-assisted self-assembly, and their predominant characteristics, including the microscopic well-dispersed and regular globular shapes with the small particle sizes of 143 nm - 170 nm and the high loading capacities of 9-12%, the amorphous form of DOX encapsulated in micelles, the low critical micelle concentration of 23.1-31.6 μg/mL, and extremely sustained in-vitro release, were shown. Among them, the desoxycytidine (DCD) conjugated micelles (DCD-CS-SB@DOX) exhibited the highest oral bioavailability of 391% versus DOX·HCl. The enhanced absorption based on the nucleoside transporter-mediation, and the dual inhibition of PYN-CS-SB micelles on P-gp efflux and CYP3A4 enzyme, was confirmed by cellular uptake, immunofluorescence, enzyme activity inhibition test. The findings showed the extensive potential of intestinal nucleoside transporter mediated PYN-CS-SB micelles in oral drug delivery.

title: Rheology-guided experimental design of dynamically crosslinked keratin/ι-carrageenan hydrogels as potential drug delivery systems
abstract: This study establishes a deterministic framework for designing 3D-printable, dynamically crosslinked hydrogel inks for controlled drug delivery via Direct Ink Writing (DIW). By blending cysteine-S-sulfonated keratin with 𝜄 -carrageenan through 𝖢 𝖺 2 + ionotropic gelation, shear-responsive networks were created. A Design of Experiments (DoE) approach generated a predictive rheology-to-printability map correlating composition with storage modulus ( 𝐺 ′ ), flow stress ( 𝜏 𝑓 ), and printability index ( 𝑃 𝑟 ). Advanced Large Amplitude Oscillatory Shear (LAOS) profiling revealed a transition from ductile, entanglement-driven networks in keratin-rich blends to brittle yielding via cooperative ionic junction rupture in crosslinked systems. Sequence of Physical Processes (SPP) analysis further identified an intracycle recovery loss factor ( t a n ⁡ 𝛿 r e c ) that dictates post-deposition shape retention. . Structural analyses verified that 𝖢 𝖺 2 + drives network compaction and crystalline 𝛽 -sheet reorganization. Crucially, dexamethasone (Dex) loading acts as a dual-functional modulator via supramolecular hydrogen bonding: behaving as an interfacial sliding agent that reduces interchain friction within densely crosslinked matrices, while acting as a secondary physical crosslinker in weakly crosslinked networks, which amplifies elastic energy storage and induces viscous Lissajous-Bowditch loop expansions. Finally, mathematical modeling confirmed that ionic crosslinking shifts drug transport from anomalous diffusion to a relaxation-controlled Super Case II regime governed by the relaxation rate ( 𝑘 𝑟 ).

title: Injectable shape-adaptive cellulose hydrogel with antibacterial activity for diabetic wound therapy
abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are chronically trapped in persistent bacterial infection and prolonged inflammation, severely hindering tissue regeneration. However, developing hydrogel dressings that can simultaneously provide effective antibacterial function and reliable biosafety remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a shape-conformable and antibacterial hydrogel dressing constructed through dynamic coordination between endogenous histidine ligand and low-toxicity Ce 3+ for infected diabetic wound repair. Histidine is covalently grafted onto carboxymethyl cellulose to obtain histidine-modified carboxymethyl cellulose, and the hydrogels are rapidly formed by simple mixing with Ce(NO 3 ) 3 solution. Reversible coordination between Ce 3+ and carboxyl, hydroxyl, and imidazole groups on cellulose chains endow exceptional injectability, rapid self-healing and shape-conformability, enabling conformal filling of irregular wound cavities. Moreover, the hydrogels exhibit antibacterial activity (exceeding 99.99%) against Escherichia coli (E. coli), Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), primarily by disrupting bacterial membrane integrity. Notably, the hydrogels show favorable cytocompatibility, with no systemic toxicity in major organs. Importantly, the hydrogel can significantly accelerate infected diabetic wound closure by reducing bacterial burden, alleviating inflammation, and promoting tissue remodeling. Overall, this simple and safe strategy provides a promising platform for antibacterial and advanced dressing design for the healing of infected diabetic wounds.

title: Low-solid content cellulose nanofiber/mixed-linkage glucan hydrogels for drug delivery and nanoparticle encapsulation
abstract: It is well established that polymer concentration significantly influences drug diffusion. However, achieving mechanically stable networks at low solid content while maintaining sustained and controlled release remains challenging. In this work, we prepared hydrogels composed of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TCNF) and mixed-linkage β-glucan (MLG) at total solid contents of 0.4% (w/w). Rheological characterization confirmed solid-like viscoelastic behavior, while FTIR, WAXS, and SEM analyses supported the formation of a physically crosslinked nanofibrillar network with a highly porous structure. Drug release studies revealed sustained release behavior governed by molecular size and charge. Compounds with lower molecular weight (4 kDa FITC-dextrans) or negative charge (ketoprofen) exhibited rapid release, reaching cumulative release rates of over 90% within 6-8 h. In contrast, higher molecular weight compounds (40 kDa FITC-dextrans) or positively charged molecules (nadolol) showed slower release profiles, with approximately 70% cumulative release after 24 h. Furthermore, the TCNF/MLG hydrogels exhibited strong retention of liposomal nanocarriers and enabled externally triggered release through the incorporation of light-sensitive liposomes, with the hydrogel matrix effectively converting rapid liposomal release into a sustained profile. Overall, this study evaluated the ability of TCNF/MLG hydrogels for controlled drug delivery applications and highlighted the potential for developing novel therapeutic strategies.

title: Structure–property relationships and hydrated-matrix-mediated aromatic guest inclusion in renatured β-1,3-1,6-glucan nanoparticles
abstract: Renatured β-1,3-1,6-glucan nanoparticles (r-glucan NPs) are hydrated polysaccharide nanostructures formed by alkali dissociation and neutralization-induced renaturation of glucan chains. Unlike rigid molecular hosts, their guest-accommodating environments are flexible, heterogeneous, and water-accessible. Here, aromatic guest incorporation into r-glucan NPs was investigated using resveratrol as a model guest for solvent-exchange analysis and 32 stilbene, azobenzene, and cinnamic acid derivatives as molecular probes. Solvent-exchange experiments showed that acetone-dependent loading conditions affected resveratrol retention, the transient colloidal state of r-glucan NPs, the recovered-complex state, and the chiral organization of retained resveratrol. Descriptor-based analysis revealed that guest molar fraction was positively associated with polarity- and hydrogen-bonding-related descriptors, including tPSA, OH count, and dipole moment, whereas logP and hydrophobic surface area showed negative correlations. Pairwise two-descriptor regression identified the logP/OH count model as the most chemically interpretable descriptor combination, highlighting the need to suppress excessive hydrophobic self-association while enabling hydroxy-group-derived stabilization. These results support a model in which aromatic guest incorporation is governed by kinetic selection during solvent exchange followed by stabilization within a hydrated glucan matrix. This study clarifies the inclusion characteristics of flexible hydrated polysaccharide matrices and provides descriptor-guided design principles for aromatic guest incorporation into r-glucan NPs.

title: Editorial to the virtual special issue: “Emerging innovators in polysaccharide science”
Purified polysaccharides from safflower (Carthamus tinctorius L.) post-extraction residues alleviate immunosuppression in mice by modulating gut microbiome
abstract: A novel polysaccharide AES-S was extracted from safflower post-extraction residues using response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural network (ANN) optimization techniques, and was purified to obtain a homogeneous polysaccharide. Structural analysis revealed that AES-S is an RG-I-type pectic polysaccharide with a backbone of →4)-α-GalpA-(1 → 2)-α-Rhap-(1 → and a molecular weight (Mw) of 16.27 kDa. AES-S restored the immune homeostasis of cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced immunosuppressed mice by promoting cytokine secretion, recovering T cell proliferation, increasing immunoglobulins and maintaining intestinal barrier integrity. Based on a pseudo-sterility mouse model and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), a crucial role of the gut microbiome and its associated metabolites in protective effects of AES-S against intestinal injury was confirmed. 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing showed that AES-S remodeled the gut microbiome, enriching beneficial bacteriota (Corynebacterium) and mycobiota (Rhodotorula). Metabolomics further revealed key changes in immunomodulatory metabolites, including 5-methylthio-d-ribose and D-galactose 6-sulfate, as well as a marked increase in short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). Correlation analyses linked these microbial shifts to metabolic recovery. These findings demonstrate that AES-S exerts immunomodulatory effects via the gut microbiome-metabolism axis, positioning it as a promising natural immunomodulatory agent.

title: Enzymatic preparation and functional development of agaro-oligosaccharides: Advances in structure–function relationships and application challenges
abstract: Agaro-oligosaccharides (AGOS), derived from agar depolymerization, are marine-derived functional carbohydrates with diverse structures and promising bioactivities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory effects. Enzymatic degradation is an attractive strategy for AGOS production due to its mild conditions, high selectivity, and ability to preserve functional groups. However, the rational preparation of structurally defined AGOS remains challenging because product profiles are determined by complex interactions among agarase catalytic architecture, substrate recognition, substrate properties, and reaction conditions. This review summarizes the catalytic characteristics of agarases and their roles in determining AGOS structural diversity. We then discuss the challenges in establishing reliable structure-function relationships, as many reported bioactivities remain based on phenotypic observations and lack direct mechanistic validation. Finally, we highlight key barriers limiting AGOS applications, including scalable production, quality control, gastrointestinal fate, and human validation. An enzyme-structure-function framework is proposed to guide the rational production and application of structurally defined AGOS.

title: Amylopectin chain length distribution and starch physicochemical properties in a glutinous rice mutant panel: A PLSR study using different chain length classification methods
abstract: A glutinous rice cultivar and its 11 derived amino acid substitution mutants of starch synthase IIIa (SSIIIa) and branching enzyme IIb (BEIIb) were investigated for the contributions of amylopectin chain length distributions (CLDs) to starch physicochemical properties. The CLDs quantified using four commonly adopted classification methods exhibited substantial and fraction-specific variations among the mutants. The partial least squares (PLS) regression models for relationships between CLDs and starch physicochemical properties exhibited satisfactory predictive ability, as indicated by Q 2 (cum) over 0.5 for the majority (19/24) of models. Regression coefficients and loading plots revealed that short branch-chain fractions were positively correlated with relative crystallinity and lamellar peak intensity, while negatively correlated with lamellar distance, gelatinization temperature, and gelatinization enthalpy. In contrast, average chain length (ACL) and long branch-chain fractions exhibited opposite trends. Very short branch-chain fractions showed positive correlations with high-temperature swelling power and setback viscosity, whereas medium-long branch-chain fractions were negatively correlated with high-temperature swelling power, setback viscosity, and breakdown viscosity, but positively correlated with hot viscosity. Furthermore, longer branch-chain fractions and increased ACL tended to elevate resistant starch while reducing slowly digestible starch. Notably, PLS discriminant analysis based on CLDs effectively distinguished ssIIIa mutants from beIIb mutants within the mutation population.

title: Versatile carboxymethyl cellulose-based pH responsive hydrogel with robust mechanical strength, adhesion, and self-healing for motion monitoring and touchscreen interaction
abstract: Hydrogels exhibiting functional properties like mechanical strength, self-healing ability, strong adhesion, and reliable sensing performance remains a major challenge for wearable electronics. Herein, a sustainable biomass-derived CPAT hydrogel was fabricated from carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), acrylic acid (AA), and tannic acid (TA) through UV-induced polymerization and supramolecular crosslinking. The cooperative integration of a poly(ethylene glycol)diacrylate crosslinked poly(acrylic acid) (PAA-PEGDA) network with dynamic hydrogen-bonding interactions generated a robust multi-network architecture. This material exhibited good stretchability, high tensile strength, and toughness. Furthermore, the hydrogel demonstrated efficient self-healing with a healing efficiency exceeding 90%, an elastic recovery of approximately 90%, and 96% stress retention after repeated deformation cycles. The hydrogel displayed strong universal adhesion, pronounced pH-responsive swelling and sensing behaviour. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed an ionic conductivity of 3.33 × 10 - -2 S cm -1 , while stable sensing performance was maintained over 1000 loading-unloading cycles. The hydrogel enabled real-time monitoring of human motions and good physiological activities, including swallowing and speech-related throat movements. The material exhibited excellent cytocompatibility, maintaining approximately 93% viability of L929 fibroblast cells. These results show the potential use of CPAT hydrogel as a multifunctional platform for wearable sensors, human-machine interfaces, and intelligent healthcare application.

title: Cooperative β-cyclodextrin/TBD acylation/deacylation in the ring-opening of ε-caprolactone – a 1H NMR and MALDI MS kinetic study
abstract: Cyclodextrins (CDs) are widely employed in supramolecular chemistry for their ability to form inclusion complexes, yet the connection between cyclic ester complexation and its influence on ring-opening processes remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the ring-opening oligomerization of ε-caprolactone (ε-CL) in the presence of β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and 1,5,7-triazabicyclo[4.4.0]dec-5-ene (TBD). The monomer conversion proceeds via monomer acylation to form cyclodextrin-oligocaprolactone intermediates, followed by their deacylation to homooligoesters. Complementary 1 H NMR and MALDI MS kinetic analyses were used to simultaneously monitor the distribution of monomer fractions. The kinetic study took into consideration the influence of β-CD, TBD, and the relative amounts in the feed. Special attention is given to the influence of the cyclodextrin structure (α-, β-, γ-CD, and TMS-β-CD - a 6-O-tert-butyldimethylsilyl-substituted β-CD). The obtained results reveal that the two hydroxyl rims of β-CD perform distinct functions. The secondary C2,3 rim acts as the reactive catalytic face, undergoing selective acylation and deacylation, whereas the primary C6 rim serves as a stabilization site reached through intramolecular C2,3/C6 acyl migration, regenerating the reactive C2,3 hydroxyls. Blocking this migration suppresses active-site regeneration and polymer formation. These findings establish the molecular basis of β-CD pseudo-enzymatic behavior and provide mechanistic principles for designing carbohydrate-based catalysts.

title: Liquid-free ion-conductive elastomers with bioinspired oriented structures based on bacterial cellulose for dual-mode humidity sensing and energy harvesting
abstract: A detection system that integrates flexibility, dual-modal humidity sensing, and self-powering capability is crucial for real-time monitoring of human holistic health. However, the disordered ion transport pathway restricts the versatility and application range of liquid-free ion conductive elastomer (ICEs). This study prepared an ICE with a biomimetic-oriented structure using bacterial cellulose, in which bacterial cellulose serves as the orientation skeleton to provide a fast ion transport channel, thereby integrating bimodal humidity response and self-powering capability. The optimized transport channels imparted high ion conductivity (0.122 S m -1 ) to the material, which is 52.6 times higher than the control sample with disordered structure. The material exhibits an excellent elongation at break (609%) and outstanding toughness (16.05 MJ m -3 ). Due to the synergistic effect of the oriented structure and the hygroscopicity of bacterial cellulose, the material demonstrates excellent humidity responsiveness for respiratory monitoring and moisture-enabled electricity generation with excellent output voltage (1.02 V), power density (19.1 mW m -2 ), and scalability. Furthermore, the material can achieve dual-modal monitoring of voltage and resistance signals, improving the accuracy of electrical signals. This work provides an optimization strategy for developing a novel biomimetic multifunctional ICEs sensor, which facilitates health monitoring and energy harvesting.

title: Methylene chain length regulates the interfacial behavior of fatty-acylated starches and its role in forming robust superhydrophobic cryogels
abstract: Developing bio-based superhydrophobic adsorbents requires a molecular understanding of how hydrophobic modifiers regulate polysaccharide wettability. However, the role of methylene-chain extension in determining the interfacial spreading behavior of fatty-acylated starch remains poorly understood. In this work, corn starches were esterified with fatty acyl chlorides of different chain lengths (C10-C18) to reveal the chain-length-dependent mechanism of hydrophobicity and to construct starch-based superhydrophobic cryogels. Structural analyses confirmed successful fatty acylation, mainly at the C6 and C2 hydroxyls. Although the degree of substitution decreased with increasing chain length, the water contact angle (WCA) increased from 62.4° to 136.9°, indicating that hydrophobicity was not governed by substitution level alone. At comparable substitution degrees, longer chains decreased the critical micelle concentration and increased surface excess concentration, supporting stronger hydrophobic association and interfacial enrichment of the long-chain derivatives. The interfacial parameters provided indirect structural evidence for the molecular arrangement of the fatty-acyl chains. Texture profile analysis identified the palmitoylated starch cryogel as the optimal substrate. After SiO₂ deposition, SC-C16@20:7@SiO₂ exhibited superhydrophobicity (WCA = 152.1°, sliding angle (SA) = 5.7°). The material had also exhibited particulate self-cleaning behavior, resistance to short-term mud contamination and the tested mechanical damage.

title: Scalable green synthesis of high-aspect-ratio cellulose nanofibers via integrated acid hydrolysis and mechanical fibrillation
Sustainable synthesis of cellulose malate ester to prepare nanocellulose paired with zwitterionic amino acid counterion
abstract: State of the art chemistry for preparation of cellulose nanofibrils (CNF) has mainly been TEMPO-mediated oxidation or carboxymethylation. In this study, CNF of high aspect ratio at high yield is prepared through synthesis of cellulose ester by using malic acid coupled with mechanical processing, yielding transparent gels and films. Ester formation is performed in an oven-based process and catalyzed by basic salts which allows for easy synthesis, without organic solvents or toxic chemicals, while on average reaching a maximum degree of substitution of 0.3 and a total charge of 1.5 mmol/g. Hydrolysis of the cellulose is limited, retaining a high molecular weight. The results indicate that crosslinking of the cellulose does not occur, even at elevated temperatures of 130 °C. A novel concept to utilize unconventional weak bases such as the amino acid lysine as counterion to the carboxylic acid in the nanocellulose is also presented, thereby introducing zwitterionic counterions. It is also shown that other organic acids such as e.g. tartaric- and glutaric acid may also be used through the same process as malic acid, opening up for a library of organic cellulose esters.

title: Light-driven innovations: Photoactive cellulose hybrids and their emerging applications
abstract: The growing interest in light-responsive technologies has led to significant advancements in photoactive hybrids, addressing critical needs across various fields, including medicine, electronics, energy, and environmental safety. Central to these innovations are photoactive materials, which enable functions such as light-driven sensing, photocatalysis, self-sterilization, and self-cleaning. In particular, technologies that improve the quality of air and water are increasingly needed, as reflected by policymakers. Recent research has focused on integrating photoactive compounds into cellulose, a renewable, mechanically robust, and easily processed biopolymer. This integration has resulted in a new class of cellulose-based photoactive hybrids that combine structural versatility and sustainability with enhanced photoactivity, stability, recyclability, and tunable functionality. These hybrids offer greener alternatives to traditional materials, supporting high-performance applications while reducing environmental impact. This review presents a comprehensive overview of fabrication strategies for photoactive cellulose hybrids and highlights their applications in water purification, antimicrobial surfaces, self-cleaning technologies, and advanced sensing platforms, while also providing insights into challenges and future directions.

title: Modified rice protein-polysaccharide complexes as stabilizers for high internal phase emulsions in application of 3D printing and β-carotene delivery
abstract: This research investigated how the phosphorylation followed by polysaccharide complexation regulated the stabilization of rice protein (RP)-based high internal phase emulsion (HIPE) and improved its 3D printability. The phosphorylation modification reduced particle size of RP and increased its solubility. Xanthan gum (XG), guar gum (GG) or sodium alginate (SA) further dose-dependently (0.05-0.2%) improved the rheological and printing performance of the HIPEs, and the effects followed XG > GG > SA. There was strong electrostatic repulsion between highly electronegative XG and phosphorylated RP (PRP), resulting in the smallest particle size and the highest solubility. This promoted a higher interfacial protein adsorption (63-70%) and effectively lowered the flocculation degree, endowing the HIPE inks with superior anti-deformation ability under large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) and the best thixotropic recovery (74-83%) and printing accuracy (86-99%). Additionally, XG and GG may enhance rigidity by forming weak gel networks and inter-chain entanglements separately. The PRP-SA complexes had lower interfacial activity, leading to poorer rheological properties and printability of the HIPEs. The modified ink also exhibited potential for delivering β-carotene (encapsulation efficiency >95% and bioaccessibility >56%), providing a basis for 3D printing-based precision nutrition. This study expands the application of RP in functional food ingredients.

title: Light-responsive liposomes for on-demand degradation of cellulose-based hydrogels
abstract: Nanocellulose hydrogels have limited biodegradability under physiological conditions, restricting applications that require controlled scaffold degradation or removal. Here, we present a light-triggered liposomal hydrogel platform that enables localized, on-demand release of cellulase enzyme to induce controlled degradation of anionic cellulose nanofiber (aCNF) hydrogels and cellulose-polysaccharide interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) hydrogels. Cellulase was encapsulated in reactive oxygen species (ROS)-sensitive stimuli-responsive liposomes containing a photosensitizer and incorporated into a hydrogel matrix, allowing external light illumination to trigger enzyme release. To preserve cellulase activity, we established a liposome preparation workflow by systematically assessing formulation and processing parameters that influence enzyme stability. Following light activation and 24 h of incubation under physiological conditions, reducing-sugar levels reached approximately 34% and 40% of the corresponding positive-control levels for the aCNF and IPN liposomal hydrogel systems, respectively. To understand ROS-induced liposome membrane destabilization, a lipid bilayer exposed to hydrogen peroxide was analyzed using high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), revealing time- and concentration-dependent degradation. Overall, the developed platform enables externally triggered cellulase-mediated degradation of hydrogels while protecting the enzyme prior to activation, providing a strategy to overcome the limited physiological degradability of cellulose-based scaffolds.

title: Utilising α-picoline-borane for the reductive amination of dextran: synthesis of polysaccharide block copolymers by reversible addition-fragmentation chain-transfer polymerisation
abstract: Polysaccharide block copolymers are often prepared by functionalisation at the polysaccharide reducing end using toxic reducing agents such as NaCNBH 3 , before incorporation of a second polymer block. Herein we report the synthesis of a polysaccharide (dextran) macromolecular chain transfer agent (macro-CTA) using the non-toxic reducing agent α-picoline-borane (pic-BH 3 ). The reductive amination reaction conditions of dextran (M r ≈ 6000 g/mol), Dex 6K , with benzylamine were optimised with conversions up to ~96%, validating the suitability of pic-BH 3 . Reaction with fluoresceinamine confirmed the use of pic-BH 3 for selective labelling at the reducing chain-end, characterised by UV–Vis spectroscopy and UV–Vis SEC analyses. When preparing a dextran macro-CTA, a diamine was used, followed by esterification with 4-cyano-4-(phenylcarbonothioylthio)pentanoic acid, yielding Dex 6K -RAFT. Novel double-hydrophilic block copolymers were synthesised by chain extending Dex 6K -RAFT with poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate (POEGMEM) by aqueous reversible addition-fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) solution polymerisation, targeting degrees of polymerisation between 50 and 200. High conversions were obtained (95–97%) after 6 h, with aqueous SEC analyses confirming successful chain extension. This work demonstrates pic-BH 3 as a non-toxic reducing agent for the aqueous chain end functionalisation of polysaccharides by reductive amination, and previously unexplored double hydrophilic Dex 6K - b -POEGMEM block copolymers, enabling safer, greener syntheses for the development of advanced polysaccharide-based materials.

title: Editorial: The 10th Biennial Meeting on Microbial Carbohydrates (BMMC)
Adaptive laboratory evolution of Komagataeibacter nataicola for formate-tolerant bacterial cellulose biosynthesis and altered membrane properties
abstract: Formate is a representative weak-acid inhibitor in lignocellulosic hydrolysates and impairs bacterial cellulose (BC) fermentation. Here, adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) was used to improve formate tolerance in Komagataeibacter nataicola DHU-1 under a defined formate-stress model. Parental DHU-1 was strongly inhibited at ≥30 mM formate, with almost unchanged glucose and formate concentrations and no recoverable BC. After 82 weeks of ALE, the evolved strain DHU-1-F exhibited tolerance to 300 mM formate. Under the tested conditions, no statistically significant changes in the measured fermentation traits were observed after 20 consecutive passages in formate-free medium. Under 300 mM formate, extracellular formate decreased by 164.94 mM within 7 days, while DHU-1-F produced 2.51 g/L BC, corresponding to 71.31% of its formate-free BC-producing capacity. Transcriptomic and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction analyses implicated membrane remodeling, respiratory and redox regulation, transport adaptation, and tetrahydrofolate-linked one‑carbon metabolism. Resequencing identified five candidate mutations shared by three isolates from a single ALE population, including a truncating mutation in an EAL domain-containing protein. The resulting BC retained its cellulose I structure but showed increased transparency, a more open nanofibrous morphology, lower apparent bulk density, and reduced mechanical strength. These findings established a strain-level strategy for formate-tolerant BC biosynthesis under defined formate-stress conditions and supported evaluation in authentic or synthetic lignocellulosic hydrolysates containing mixed inhibitors.

title: Chitosan/gellan gum nanofiber-reinforced PVA films with photothermal tellurium nanoparticles for strawberry preservation
abstract: In this study, chitosan/gellan gum (CS/GG) polyelectrolyte complex nanofibers prepared by ultrasound-assisted exfoliation and pomelo peel extract-catalyzed tellurium nanoparticles (PPE-TeNPs) were incorporated into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix to develop photothermal active packaging films. The optimized PVA film, containing 3 wt% CS/GG nanofibers and 3 wt% PPE-TeNPs, exhibited a tensile strength of 35.21 ± 0.72 MPa, an elongation at break of 80.22 ± 1.81%, a water vapor permeability of 8.95 × 10 -11 g·Pa -1 ·s -1 ·m -1 , and a carbon dioxide permeability of 0.78 × 10 -7 g·m -1 ·s -1 . Under 808 nm NIR irradiation, the film surface reached 59.5 °C, achieving antibacterial rates of 99.61% against S. aureus and 98.28% against E. coli, while reducing the colony diameter of Botrytis cinerea by 99.42%. During strawberry storage, the temperature of the fruit surface beneath the film reached only 35.88 °C, while PCG3-Te 3 -NIR treatment maintained a lower respiration rate and malondialdehyde content and greater catalase activity and vitamin C retention, effectively delaying spoilage during 8 days of storage at 25 °C. Total tellurium migration remained below 0.39 mg/kg in all four food simulants throughout the 10-day test. These results demonstrate the potential of CS/GG nanofiber-reinforced PPE-TeNP-functionalized PVA films for photothermal strawberry preservation.

title: Gelatinization differentially impacts in vitro fermentation of high-amylose maize starch
abstract: Some of the starch in a meal, depending on how it was thermally processed, may escape complete digestion in the upper gut and pass into the colon as available for microbial fermentation. This study uses an in vitro batch fecal model to examine the fermentability of high-amylose maize starch (HAMS) that has been gelatinized to different degrees (DG). Compared with native HAMS, more gases and acids were produced from gelatinized HAMS during the initial 4 h of fermentation, which was attributed to the stronger binding of bacteria to gelatinized HAMS. At the endpoint of fermentation, HAMS and HAMS with a DG of 22.8% (DG22.8) yielded more butyrate, whereas HAMS with DG ≥ 45.5 generated more acetate and propionate. The characteristics of SCFA production from fermentations of HAMS with different DG were associated with the enrichment of specific SCFA-producing bacterial species. There were no apparent differences in gas and acid production, and composition of the microbiota, in fermentations of HAMS with DG ≥ 45.5, although proliferation of pathobionts (Escherichia_Shigella and Collinsella) was noted compared to HAMS and HAMS-DG22.8. Our study showed that the amount of gelatinized starch in the fermentation substrate significantly affected fermentation behavior, with higher proportions of gelatinized starch available for colonic fermentation potentially having negative effects on the gut health.

title: Dry roller-milled yellow pea and chickpea flours with high cotyledon cell integrity reduce starch digestibility
abstract: The objectives of this study were to use dry roller milling to produce pulse flours varying in cell integrity and develop food ingredients with controlled starch digestibility. Yellow peas and chickpeas were milled into flours with coarse-, medium-, and small-sized particles (with volume-weighted mean particle sizes of ~940, 400 and 150 μm) but having essentially the same composition. These flours were analyzed for morphology, thermal properties, pasting characteristics, and in vitro starch digestibility. Raw coarse-sized flours retained more intact cotyledon cells as observed by confocal laser scanning microscopy, resulting in high resistant starch (RS) (~50%) and low rapidly digestible starch (RDS) contents. Upon cooking, the RS content decreased and the RDS content increased in all flours, but the coarse-sized yellow pea and chickpea flours still retained higher RS (~25-30%) and lower RDS contents compared with the medium- and small-sized flours. Coarse-sized flours exhibited the highest gelatinization temperatures and the lowest pasting viscosities because of intact cotyledon cells inhibiting starch swelling. These findings demonstrate that dry roller milling can be used as a scalable processing strategy to preserve cotyledon cell integrity and develop pulse ingredients with reduced starch digestibility.

title: Structural complexity and biofunctional properties of highly sulfated carrageenan–agaroid galactans from Calliblepharis fimbriata: Insights from selective chemical modifications
abstract: Galactans isolated from Calliblepharis fimbriata were characterized using selective chemical modification approaches coupled with 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy to elucidate their structural complexity and structure-activity relationships. The polysaccharides comprised mixed d and l-galactopyranosyl residues associated with ι-carrageenan (G4S - DA2S) and porphyran (G - L6S) motifs. 1 H 13 C HSQC analysis of chemically desulfated derivatives revealed preferential removal of sulfate groups at C-4, while DA2S and L6S units remained largely preserved, yielding α-carrageenan (G - DA2S) segments. Alkali treatment induced partial cyclization of precursor residues, and the principal fraction exhibited a molar ratio of d-galactose, 3,6-anhydrogalactose, and sulfate ester of 1.00:0.04:0.36. Structure-activity relationship analysis suggested that sulfate substitution at C-2 and C-4 positions contributed to an enhanced anticoagulant activity, and high anionic moieties were further associated with increased inhibition of α-glucosidase (38.2-68.8%) and α-amylase (15.3-86%). Furthermore, the galactans exhibited non-cytotoxicity toward RAW264.7 macrophages at concentrations below 32 μg/mL and significantly enhanced (p < 0.05) phagocytic activity and nitric oxide production in a concentration-dependent manner, indicating an immunostimulatory potential through macrophage activation. Overall, these findings reveal the structural complexity of C. fimbriata galactans and establish clear links between their distinct sulfation patterns and biological functions, providing a basis for their potential biomedical and nutraceutical applications.

title: A comprehensive review of chitin/chitosan-derived antimicrobial materials: Structural design, structure–activity relationships and applications
abstract: This review covers the preparation strategies of chitin/chitosan derivatives and their impact on material properties, the peptide-coupling chemistries and their synergistic roles in constructing chitosan-antimicrobial peptide systems, and the development of metal/inorganic, organic and natural extract-based composites with enhanced physical, chemical and biological properties. To clarify these diverse material systems, this review systematically discusses a variety of antibacterial pathways, including membrane destruction, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, metal-ion release and chelation-induced ionic imbalance, metabolic inhibition and gene expression interference. Different from previous reviews that mainly focused on a single material type, antimicrobial mechanism or application field, this review highlights the relationships among structural design, antimicrobial mechanisms and application-specific suitability. Herein, we summarize the key challenges and future opportunities, with a focus on scalable production, elucidation of structure-activity relationships, and application-oriented material design. The review covers: i) derivatization strategies of chitin/chitosan materials and the effects on properties; ii) design and functional principles of chitosan-antimicrobial peptide conjugates; iii) integrating antimicrobial mechanisms across different chitin/chitosan materials; iv) representative applications in food, biomedicine, and environmental remediation. This review aims to provide design guidance for next-generation chitin/chitosan-derived antimicrobial materials.

title: Multifunctional nonwovens: assessing the performance of lignin-modified regenerated cellulose fibres
abstract: Multifunctional lyocell fibres modified with lignin were obtained by co-dissolving hardwood sulphite pulp and eucalyptus kraft lignin (EKL) (9: 1 mass ratio) in N-methylmorpholine-N-oxide/H₂O (ca. 10% by weight of solids), followed by dry-jet wet spinning. The addition of EKL to the dope did not significantly affect its viscoelastic properties, spinning behaviour, or final fibre strength. Lignin occurrence in the fibres was assessed by confocal Raman spectroscopy. Laboratory nonwovens were manufactured using pilot carding and needle-punching machines. Thermally pre-treated nonwovens exhibited increased hydrophobicity, with water contact angles exceeding 120°. Fabrics produced from lyocell-type blended fibres exhibited excellent UV protection factor (UPF 50+), effective thermal management, and antimicrobial activity against S. aureus. These results highlight lignin as a multifunctional bio-based additive for man-made cellulose fibres, compatible with wet spinning and textile manufacturing processes, and confirm the suitability of cellulose-lignin blended fibres for a wide range of applications, from functional to technical textiles.

title: Advances in plant polysaccharide-based self-healing hydrogels
abstract: Traditional hydrogels suffer from irreversible structural damage under mechanical stress, which shortens service lifetimes and restricts their practical deployment in dynamic scenarios. Self-healing hydrogels constructed from plant-derived polysaccharides stand out against synthetic polymers and other biopolymers as promising biomaterials, owing to their abundant terrestrial resources, favorable biocompatibility, and inherent biodegradability. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in self-healing hydrogels based on major plant polysaccharides, including cellulose, hemicellulose, starch, galactomannans and their derivatives. The review explores the molecular design principles and intrinsic self-healing mechanisms of these polysaccharide systems, and compares how chemical structures of different plant polysaccharides impact healing efficiency and mechanical properties. The merits and demerits of each polysaccharide type are discussed with respect to solubility, mechanical robustness, gelation characteristics, and long-term stability. Additionally, the review identifies key challenges currently confronting the field, including the intrinsic trade-off between self-healing efficiency and mechanical strength, inadequate long-term stability under complex physiological conditions, cumbersome modification procedures, and limited scalability for large-scale production. Future research endeavors should prioritize the modification of polysaccharide molecular structures, innovative cross-linked network construction, and computational modeling to predict structure-property relationships, thereby facilitating the application of plant polysaccharide in high value-added fields.

title: Equipping chitosan cryogels with a silicon armor for integrated elasticity, hydrophobicity, and flame retardancy
abstract: Chitosan cryogels, characterized by highly porous and lightweight architectures, offer the advantages of renewability and excellent biocompatibility, but their inherent brittleness, poor moisture resistance, and limited thermal stability severely restrict practical applications. Herein, a "silicon armor" strategy was developed by employing hyperbranched epoxy silicone resin (HESR) as a chemical bridge to construct a covalently bonded silicon-containing hybrid shell on the chitosan framework through epoxy-amine ring-opening reactions. Benefiting from the abundant reactive epoxy groups, the hybrid shell further enabled the multiscale integration of functional components. An inner-outer dual‑phosphorus flame-retardant architecture was established by incorporating melamine polyphosphate (MPP) and diethyl phosphoramidate (DEPA), while the Si-O-Si network simultaneously contributed to structural reinforcement and thermal stability. In addition, polyetheramine flexible segments introduced entropy elasticity into the hybrid network, effectively alleviating the intrinsic brittleness of the rigid silicon framework and improving its deformation recovery capability. Subsequent hydrophobic modification further reduced the surface energy and significantly enhanced the moisture resistance and environmental stability of the cryogel. As a result, the obtained CS-Si cryogel integrates efficient flame retardancy, excellent elasticity, mechanical robustness, thermal insulation, and hydrophobic protection into a single biomass-derived system, providing a simple, efficient, and versatile strategy for the design of multifunctional sustainable cryogel materials.

title: Ultrasensitive probes for magnetic resonance angiography by renal-clearable macrocyclic gadolinium complex-grafted cross-linked dextran nanospheres
Multiscale ion transport channels based on chitosan and nanocellulose: Synergistic enhancement of mechanical properties and ionic conductivity, and multifunctional integration
abstract: Eutectogels are promising in flexible wearable electronics, but the inherent trade-off between mechanical strength and ionic conductivity limits their development. Here, we introduced polyethyleneimine-modified cellulose nanocrystals (PEI@CNC) and chitosan (CS) into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix, and constructed a PVA composite eutectogel (PCxSy) with an aligned lamellar porous structure via directional freezing. The anisotropic low-tortuosity channels, combined with the incorporation of PEI@CNC and CS that provide additional ion-conducting pathways, endow the material with an ionic conductivity of 0.74 S·m -1 . Meanwhile, multiple hydrogen bonds among PVA, CS, PEI@CNC, and the DES components form a dense physical network, providing excellent mechanical properties along the orientation direction, with a tensile strength of 3.60 MPa and toughness of 10.39 MJ·m -3 . The eutectogel exhibits dual-mode strain/pressure sensing with favorable cycling stability under bending, shearing, and compression. Zn 2+ from the DES synergizes with PEI@CNC and CS to impart antibacterial activity (95.71% against E. coli, 95.44% against S. aureus), effectively reducing skin infection risk during long-term wear.

title: Sodium alginate-based environmentally stable tough ionogel sensors integrated with machine learning for high-accuracy static gesture recognition
abstract: Gel materials with exceptional mechanical property, environmental stability, and reliable sensing performance are highly desirable for intelligent human-machine interfaces. However, conventional hydrogel systems generally prone to fail under load-bearing applications due to their poor mechanics, progressive dehydration, and freezing-induced performance deterioration. Herein, we report a mechanically tough ionogel with remarkable environmental stability via a facile solvent-replacement strategy: incorporating a non-volatile halometallate ionic liquid composed of CaBr 2 and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide ([BMIM]Br) into a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAAm/SA) hydrogel network. Synergistic coordination and ion-dipole interactions reconstructed the network structure and solvent-polymer microenvironment, facilitating efficient energy dissipation. Consequently, the optimized ionogel exhibited remarkable environmental stability and mechanical properties, including 2860% stretchability, 0.68 MPa tensile strength, 9.46 MJ/m 3 toughness, and 16.02 kJ/m 2 fracture energy. Moreover, the ionogel demonstrated stable electromechanical response across a broad strain range (1-500%). Benefiting from these merits, the ionogel-based sensor enabled accurate monitoring of complex human motions and achieved 99.45% recognition accuracy for eight static gestures when integrated with a machine learning algorithm. Collectively, this work provides a facile strategy for constructing environmentally stable yet mechanic tough ionogels through coordination-ionic co-regulation paradigm, offering a viable pathway towards reliable and field-deployable gel systems for wearable electronics.

title: Chitosan–sodium alginate hydrogels incorporating amino acid-derived ionic liquids as antimicrobial agents
abstract: Polysaccharide-based hydrogels have been investigated for cutaneous applications owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and ability to provide a favorable environment for wound healing. In this study, chitosan–sodium alginate (CS/Alg) hydrogels incorporating ionic liquids (ILs) derived from the decyl-1-methylimidazolinium cation ([DEC(MIM)] + ) and the amino acid anions glycine ([GLY] − ) or lysine ([LYS] − ) were developed and characterized. The effects of IL on the rheological properties and antimicrobial activity were evaluated. The formulations remained physically stable throughout the storage period while maintaining a skin-compatible pH (4.5). Scanning electron microscopy revealed irregular and porous structures favorable for topical adhesion and bioactive compound loading. Furthermore, IL incorporation increased the viscosity and mechanical strength of the CS/Alg hydrogels. Optimal rheological properties were observed for formulations containing 10% [DEC(MIM)][GLY] and 5% [DEC(MIM)][LYS]. Formulations containing 15% [DEC(MIM)][GLY] and 10–15% [DEC(MIM)][LYS] exhibited pronounced bacteriostatic and bactericidal activities. The Hen's egg chorioallantoic membrane (HET-CAM) assay indicated suitability for superficial topical application. The 1 H NMR chemical shift analysis was consistent with intermolecular interactions between ILs and polymers, which may contribute to hydrogel structuration and mechanical resistance. Overall, IL incorporation significantly influenced the physicochemical and biological properties of CS/Alg hydrogels, highlighting their potential for topical pharmaceutical applications.

title: An O-acetylated glucomannan from Bletilla striata: Structural characterization and ADP-dependent platelet-activating hemostatic activity
abstract: Previous work demonstrated that crude Bletilla striata polysaccharides exhibited hemostatic effects against gastric bleeding through the activation of ADP pathway, whereas their key homogeneous active constituent remains structurally undefined. Herein, bioactivity-guided fractionation afforded a novel homogeneous polysaccharide BSP-60 (6271 Da), identified as the core hemostatic component. Differing markedly from all reported B. striata polysaccharide, BSP-60 consists of glucose (Glcp) and mannose (Manp) at a molar ratio of 1:1.88, featuring a linear unbranched chain of regularly alternating →4)-Glcp-(1 → and →4)-Manp-(1 → linkages with a polymerization degree of 39, and O-acetyl groups substitute at C2 or C3 of Manp. Combining the results of human washed platelets and aspirin-induced rat gastric bleeding model, BSP-60 markedly activates the G protein-coupled receptors P2Y 1 and P2Y 12 to intervenes downstream PLCγ2/PKC and PI3K/Akt signaling cascades, elevating intracellular calcium mobilization, decreasing cAMP levels, and stimulating integrin αIIbβ3 activation, which improves multiple platelet functions and ultimately accelerates hemostasis. Collectively, these findings corroborate that the structurally unique BSP-60 represents the predominant ADP-dependent hemostatic mechanism. Benefiting from its linear unbranched glucomannan architecture, BSP-60 stands as an attractive lead for the development of novel gastric hemostatic drugs.

title: Spatially core-shell mussel inspired alginate hydrogel enabling adhesive outer layers and a reinforced inner network for intelligent pressure detection
abstract: Inspired by the functional partitioning of biological interfaces, we report a core-shell-structured adhesive hydrogel (SA-Dopa hydrogel) that spatially decouples interfacial adhesion from bulk mechanical reinforcement for wearable sensing applications. Conventional one-pot adhesive hydrogels generally distribute adhesive moieties throughout the entire network, leading to coupled surface/bulk functions and inefficient use of interfacial binding groups. In this design, a Ca 2+ -coordinated sodium alginate inner network serves as a mechanically robust load-bearing framework, while a catechol-rich outer hydrogel layer provides mussel-inspired surface adhesion. This structure enables strong and durable adhesion to diverse substrates, enhanced mechanical strength and toughness, and stable deformation tolerance without sacrificing interfacial compliance. The resulting hydrogel further exhibits reliable electromechanical transduction, featuring strain-dependent sensitivity. Benefiting from the synergistic coupling of a reinforced interior and adhesive outer shell, the SA-Dopa hydrogel supports accurate detection of tensile and compressive stimuli, and Morse-code-assisted wearable communication. Of particular significance, the material can be readily integrated into wireless pressure-sensing arrays and intelligent grippers, enabling real-time pressure mapping, object-shape discrimination, and adaptive grasping feedback. This work establishes a simple yet effective strategy for spatially allocating adhesion and mechanics within a single hydrogel platform, opening a new route toward high-performance wearable sensors and intelligent soft robotic interfaces.

title: Cold gelation of 4-O-methyl-D-glucurono-D-xylan in aqueous media: influence of salts on the rheological behaviour
abstract: The rheological characterization of semi-dilute aqueous solutions of 4-O-methyl-D-glucurono-D-xylan (MGX), extracted from beech wood sawdust, has evidenced a reversible cold gelation displaying a large hysteresis. As an example, for a 180 g/L MGX solution in pure water, a G"/G' crossing at 16.6 °C upon cooling has been found, leading to a gelation, and a G'/G" crossing at 38.3 °C upon heating back to the initial temperature of 50 °C, leading to a dissociation of the gel state. In this study, we demonstrate that such thermal transitions can be modulated with the MGX concentration (from 150 to 190 g/L), respectively from 11.3 to 19 °C for the cooling transition and from 30.8 to 40.5 °C for the heating transition. Gelation is also favoured with the addition of monovalent salts like LiCl, NaCl, and KCl, and more particularly with divalent salts like MgCl 2 and CaCl 2 , at the same ionic strength (0.15 M). The observed increase of MGX structuration at 10 °C in the presence of salts (notably with CaCl 2 ), and the subsequent retention of a gel state at body temperature could be useful for biomedical applications.

title: Enzymatic modification of starch: From catalytic specificity to multi-scale structure, functional properties, and applications
abstract: Starch has inherent limitations such as poor thermal stability and high retrogradation tendency, but enzymatic modification offers a mild and specific approach to precisely regulate starch structure and function, enabling the development of health-beneficial products like resistant starch. This review summarizes fundamental starch properties and key enzymes used for modification, and discusses the impact of enzymatic modification on starch morphology, multi-level structure, functional properties, and digestibility, along with practical applications in various food systems. The key findings show that enzymatic modification effectively tailors starch molecular structures-such as amylose/amylopectin ratio and chain length distribution-using specific enzymes (maltogenic amylase, branching enzyme), allowing precise modulation of swelling power, solubility, pasting characteristics, rheological behavior, and digestibility, thereby improving retrogradation resistance and freeze-thaw stability. This technology has been successfully applied in baked goods, frozen foods, and low-fat dairy products, providing a robust platform for developing novel starches with tailored properties.

title: Recent progress in cellulose membranes for ionic, molecular, and oil/water separations
abstract: Cellulose membranes offer a sustainable platform for separating ionic, molecular, and oil/water mixtures. Their crystalline nanofibrillar structure and abundant surface hydroxyls offer both a tunable pore architecture and a chemically versatile surface. This review links cellulose dissolution, membrane fabrication, and separation mechanisms into one design framework. Solvent systems were examined for how they govern dissolution and the resulting pore architecture. Fabrication technologies from dissolution-regeneration and phase inversion to melt processing and stretching, spinning, freeze-drying, and crosslinking were then compared for their control over pore structure and surface chemistry. On this basis, the mechanisms of adsorption, size sieving, Donnan exclusion, dielectric exclusion, and super-wettability were analyzed to establish structure-performance relationships. Systematic comparison of solvent systems and fabrication technologies identified the combinations best suited to specific separation targets. This review provides design principles and mechanistic insights to guide the development of next-generation cellulose membranes for water purification and resource recovery.

title: 3D-printed recyclable porous scaffolds from biomass-derived cellulose nanofibrils/carbon hybrids for tunable electromagnetic shielding
Deep eutectic solvent–derived microfibrillated cellulose from wood and agro-residues: Functionalization, energy-efficient production, and properties
abstract: Acidic deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of choline chloride and lactic acid was investigated as a pulping and activation medium for producing functional microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) from wood and agro-residue biomass. Pine and hemp were selected to evaluate DES-assisted fiber activation, fibrillation efficiency, and material properties. DES processing induced fiber swelling and surface functionalization, reducing cell wall recalcitrance and enhancing fiber accessibility during mechanical refining. Compared with kraft-processed fibers, DES-derived fibers exhibited shorter fiber lengths, increased cell wall thickness, and higher fines content, enabling high-solids MFC production with substantially lower energy input. Hemp-derived MFC achieved a ∼ 90% fines at ∼430 kWh/t, representing >90% lower specific fibrillation energy than kraft-derived MFC requiring >5000 kWh/t for comparable fibrillation. Multiscale characterization revealed progressive fibrillar development and spatial distribution of residual lignin across DES-derived MFC surfaces. Under a prospective, literature-informed assumption of 94% overall DES recovery, techno-economic analysis estimated a minimum selling price of ∼ $1680/OD ton, indicating potential economic competitiveness with conventional MFC production. Overall, DES processing provides a promising high-solids, energy-efficient pathway for producing functional MFC from diverse lignocellulosic feedstocks, with potential applications in sustainable packaging, barrier coatings, rheology modification, and bio-based composites.

title: Low-conjugation amino chromophore-stabilized oxidized cellulose for efficient room-temperature phosphorescence
abstract: Organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is typically achieved by tailoring the electronic structures of chromophore, for example, through extended π-conjugation, or by restricting nonradiative decay within the rigid microstructure. Most reported RTP systems therefore involve highly conjugated chromophores or rigid matrices, while the use of low-conjugation chromophores in bio-based frameworks remains relatively underexplored. Herein, we report an amino-chromophore-grafted design with low conjugation for stabilizing ultralong RTP in oxidized cellulose. In which, microcrystalline cellulose is selectively oxidized to dialdehyde cellulose, providing abundant aldehyde groups for the covalent grafting of amino chromophores. The resulting imine linkages and multivalent hydrogen-bonding interactions immobilize the chromophores and reconstruct a rigid local environment, thereby suppressing non-radiative decay, and stabilizing triplet excitons.
